notes: SIMDTEST has no constructor arguments. SIMDTESTHook takes (IPoolManager manager_, address token_) in that order: $poolManager resolves to Ethereum mainnet PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90 on chainId 1; $token resolves to the newly deployed SIMDTEST. Deploy the immutable hook directly with CREATE2 at an address whose low 14 bits equal 0x20c4: beforeInitialize (bit 13), beforeSwap (bit 7), afterSwap (bit 6), afterSwapReturnDelta (bit 2); all other permissions are false. Callbacks accept only the PoolManager. beforeInitialize binds the hook to its SIMDTEST/IMD pool with static LP fee 12500 (1.25%) and tickSpacing 60. initialPrice is decimal sqrtPriceX96, sqrt(currency1/currency0) times 2^96 with currencies sorted by address, recorded for provenance; the launch factory determines the opening price from launch economics. On buys and sells, afterSwap charges floor(abs(actual unspecified-currency BalanceDelta) / 100), including exact-input, exact-output and partial fills, through afterSwapReturnDelta. This 100 bps hook fee is additional to the LP fee; beforeSwap reserves nothing and never overrides the LP fee. Fees accrue as hook-owned ERC-6909 claims without transfers or buybacks inside swap callbacks. Anyone may call sweep() to redeem launched-token claims and send them, plus directly held launched tokens, to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD. executeBatch() requires a separate PoolManager unlock and allows a funded buyback at least 3600 seconds after initialization or the last batch that spent IMD. It budgets up to 25% of pending IMD, including claims and direct holdings, for an exact-input PoolManager swap. Its sole slippage guard is a sqrtPriceLimit representing a 300 bps pool-price bound, tightened against both the geometric time-weighted reference and current liquid spot; empty liquidity retains the last liquid observation or initialization tick. Partial fills leave unspent IMD accrued; there is no minimum-output check. Self-initiated batch swaps pay no hook fee and send bought tokens to the fixed burn address. Zero-spend attempts preserve lastBatch and reference history. Views: pending(), pendingBurn(), lastBatch(), referencePrice(). Fee, interval, budget and price-limit constants are fixed; there is no owner, setter, proxy or upgrade path.
